attacks.claim: The public 'Recent signers' panel renders each signer's full name and full postal code next to city, violating the agreed public-display limit (first name, last initial, city only) and exposing personal data publicly and irreversibly once visible.
attacks.evidence: • {{ s.full_name }} {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}

attacks.claim: No first-name/last-initial derivation exists in the template or in recent_signers(), and the 'What ships' section promises that truncation, so the spec and implementation contradict each other.
attacks.evidence: What ships: "showing first name + last initial and city" vs template: "{{ s.full_name }}"; ABSENT: any first-name/last-initial derivation in _recent.html or recent_signers()

attacks.claim: The newsletter/organizer-updates checkbox is pre-ticked. GDPR requires consent to be a clear affirmative act, so pre-checked consent for EU signers' organizer marketing is not valid.
attacks.evidence: <input type="checkbox" id="news" name="newsletter_opt_in" value="1" checked>

attacks.claim: Full name, email and postal code are collected from EU residents with no privacy notice, controller identity, purposes or lawful basis shown at the point of collection (GDPR Art. 13).
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no privacy notice link, processing-purpose statement or lawful-basis disclosure in the sign form template or the rollout plan

attacks.claim: Postal code is mandatory for every signer although the stated purpose is signature counting and confirmation; it is excess collection under data minimisation and is also displayed publicly.
attacks.evidence: <input id="postal" name="postal_code" required autocomplete="postal-code">

attacks.claim: Organizers can export opted-in signers' personal data as CSV with no stated processor/controller terms, lawful basis, or access/erasure handling for signers. Export field minimisation is also unverified.
attacks.evidence: Organizers can export signers who opted in to updates as CSV; export is rate-limited and audit-logged. ABSENT: data-processing terms, lawful basis or erasure/access process covering organizer CSV exports

attacks.claim: Retention and erasure are only addressed for unconfirmed rows (7-day purge); confirmed signers' email and postal code have no stated retention period or deletion path.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention period and erasure process for confirmed rows in signatures

attacks.claim: Validation errors are never written into the live region; the only 422 feedback is a red border class, so screen reader users are not told which field failed or why (WCAG 3.3.1, 4.1.3).
attacks.evidence: ... classList.add('is-invalid'); form.elements[fields[0]].focus();

attacks.claim: Invalid fields are not programmatically associated with their errors: no aria-invalid and no aria-describedby on inputs.
attacks.evidence: <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required autocomplete="email"> ... classList.add('is-invalid')

attacks.claim: Non-422 failures (409 duplicate, 500, network error) have no else branch, so no message is shown and the form gives no feedback to screen reader or keyboard users about whether the signature was recorded.
attacks.evidence: if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location'); with no else branch; QA: "Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass"

attacks.claim: Accessibility QA is limited to an automated axe-core scan with no screen reader, keyboard-only, or reflow/error-state testing, so the WCAG 2.1 AA commitment for the public flow is unverified.
attacks.evidence: | axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations | (no assistive-technology or keyboard test row)

attacks.claim: The invalid state relies mainly on a red border and pink background with no text or icon marker.
attacks.evidence: .sign-form input.is-invalid { border: 2px solid #d93025; background: #fdecea; }

attacks.claim: The client's success path reads a Location header from fetch, but fetch follows redirects automatically and hides that header from script, so window.location may be set to null on success.
attacks.evidence: if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location');

attacks.claim: The 422 handler indexes form.elements by server-supplied names without checking them or that fields is non-empty; an unexpected or empty fields array throws a TypeError and leaves the form in an error state with no message.
attacks.evidence: for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); form.elements[fields[0]].focus();

attacks.claim: Recent-signers ordering by recency is not shown in the query, so the 'most recent' claim is unverified.
attacks.evidence: petition.recent_signers(limit=20, confirmed_only=True)

attacks.claim: The signing endpoint has no described bot or abuse protection (CAPTCHA, proof-of-work, per-IP or per-email rate limit), so signatures can be scripted and petition integrity undermined.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: CAPTCHA, proof-of-work, per-IP or per-email rate limit on POST /p/{slug}/sign. The QA table only lists load at 400 signatures/s and a duplicate-email 409.

attacks.claim: The 409 duplicate response on a public endpoint reveals whether an email has already signed a petition, an enumeration oracle with no stated rate limit.
attacks.evidence: "Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass"

attacks.claim: The rollback plan covers only the form. It does not address signatures already collected, confirmation emails already sent, or PII already stored in two regions, and does not say whether the panel and CSV export are also disabled by the flag.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.

attacks.claim: QA was run on 2.4.0-rc3 but the release is 2.4.0, with no evidence that changes between rc3 and release were re-tested.
attacks.evidence: QA report summary (staging, build 2.4.0-rc3)

attacks.claim: The rollout gates only on error and bounce rates, with no abort threshold for duplicate spikes, confirmation-send failures, or Postmark rate limiting, and no kill switch for outbound email.
attacks.evidence: Watch `sign_submit_error_rate` (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.
